researcher_notes: Targeted fill-in for Xavier Becerra on California K-12 school funding. Despite Becerra being a Democratic frontrunner (tied for first in a May 2026 Democratic Party poll) with extensive published priorities, K-12 education is conspicuously absent from his campaign messaging. Searched: (1) his official priorities page, which lists 8 issue areas (Health Care, Fighting Donald Trump, Housing, Economy & Affordability, Energy & Utilities, Disaster Preparedness, AI, Homelessness) with no education section; (2) his official bio page (no K-12 mention); (3) EdSource's April 30, 2026 candidate-by-candidate education-funding comparison article, which named Becerra as a top candidate but attributed no quote or position to him on K-12 funding — a commenter on the article (Juliana Sheldon) explicitly flagged the omission as 'inexcusable'; (4) the CalMatters 2026 voter guide for governor, which lists only climate goals and utility/insurance rates as Becerra priorities; (5) the LAist long-form interview transcript with Larry Mantle, in which Becerra discusses healthcare, the budget deficit, homelessness, gas prices, immigration, labor, and pandemic preparedness but does not mention K-12, schools, teachers, Prop 98, LCFF, or school bonds at all; (6) the Local News Matters republication of the EdSource debate piece (same null result); (7) the Commonwealth Club Feb 4, 2026 event page (403 forbidden, could not verify). The California Faculty Association co-endorsed Becerra and Thurmond, but that endorsement specifically references higher education / CFA members, not K-12. No federal-vote-record evidence from his 1993–2017 congressional tenure surfaced that would unambiguously place him on the 1–5 K-12-funding scale (and such votes would be on federal Title I-style funding, not California Prop 98 / LCFF, so they would not directly resolve a state-level stance even if found). Conclusion: Becerra has not articulated a public position on California K-12 funding sufficient to place him on the 1–5 scale. Marking 'unknown' / 'insufficient_data' is the honest finding and is itself a substantive finding about his campaign focus.

positions.summary: Becerra has not published a K-12 funding position. His 2026 priorities page lists eight issue areas (health care, fighting Trump, housing, economy & affordability, energy & utilities, disaster preparedness, AI, homelessness) with no education section, and EdSource's April 30, 2026 candidate-by-candidate education-funding comparison attributed no quote or position to him on K-12 funding — an omission a commenter on the article called 'inexcusable.' He may align with the broader Democratic field's pro-funding posture, but he has offered no specific Prop 98, LCFF, teacher-pay, or school-bond commitment that would place him on the 1–5 scale.
positions.source_quote: No mention of Xavier Becerra's stances on improving education, but you include the ones from candidates polling in single digits? That's inexcusable.
positions.notes: The source_quote above is a reader-comment observation on the EdSource article, not a Becerra statement — used because the verifiable, citable fact here is the documented absence of a Becerra position in the most comprehensive 2026 K-12 funding comparison piece. Primary sources searched and confirmed silent on K-12: (1) https://www.xavierbecerra2026.com/priorities/ — eight issue pages, none on education; (2) https://www.xavierbecerra2026.com/bio/ — no K-12 mention; (3) https://calmatters.org/california-voter-guide-2026/governor/ — lists only climate goals and a utility/insurance-rate freeze as Becerra priorities; (4) https://laist.com/news/politics/2026-election-california-primary-xavier-becerra-california-governor-transcript — Larry Mantle interview covers healthcare, budget, homelessness, gas, immigration, labor, pandemic preparedness, with zero mention of K-12, schools, teachers, Prop 98, LCFF, or school bonds; (5) EdSource's comparison article names Becerra as a top candidate but attributes no K-12 quote or position to him; (6) Local News Matters republication confirms same null result. iSideWith lists charter / voucher / book-ban positions for Becerra but explicitly attributes them to 'voterbase' inference and 'ChatGPT Party Research,' not primary sources, so they are not citable. The California Faculty Association co-endorsement with Thurmond is about higher education / CFA faculty, not K-12. Federal congressional voting on Title I-style funding (1993–2017) did not surface specific evidence in searches and would in any case not directly resolve a California Prop 98 / LCFF stance. Honest finding: insufficient data.
